skill.name: amazon-competitor-analyzer
skill.description: Collects Amazon product data for supplied ASINs through the BrowserAct API and creates competitor comparison reports.
skill.summary: Analyze Amazon ASIN competitors with BrowserAct data collection and exportable reports.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill performs disclosed BrowserAct network requests and writes local analysis reports. Most high static findings are false positives for documented API-key handling or Markdown examples, but command-line API-key input and report overwrites remain real risks.

remediation.issue: BrowserAct network egress is required for every analysis run.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact BrowserAct endpoint, data sent, and API-key use before users run the skill.

remediation.issue: Report files use fixed names in the selected output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Add timestamped filenames or a no-overwrite option before writing CSV, Markdown, and structured reports.

remediation.issue: The CLI accepts BrowserAct API keys through command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment and remove or discourage --api-key usage in examples.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Accepted Through Command Line
semantic_findings.description: The CLI accepts a BrowserAct API key through --api-key, which can expose the secret in shell history or process listings. Environment variables are safer for routine use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The argument parser defines --api-key and the value is assigned before analyzer initialization. This is a common credential exposure risk even though the API key is used for a legitimate service.

content.value_statement: Manual competitor research across Amazon ASINs is slow and inconsistent. This skill collects BrowserAct product data and creates CSV, Markdown, and JSON analysis reports.
actual_capabilities: Submits supplied Amazon ASINs to a BrowserAct workflow template.
Polls BrowserAct task status until each product workflow finishes.
Exports product data to CSV, Markdown, and JSON report files.
Compares prices, ratings, review counts, brands, weight, and feature lists.
Validates ASIN format before submitting workflow tasks.
Supports an output directory for saved analysis files.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct API key and active network access.
Depends on BrowserAct workflow results and Amazon page availability.
The built-in analysis is limited to basic price, rating, and review comparisons.
Report files use fixed names and can overwrite prior outputs in the target directory.

use_cases.title: Compare Rival Listings
use_cases.description: Review price, rating, review volume, and feature differences across competing Amazon ASINs.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Product Specs
use_cases.description: Collect structured product details before updating specifications, positioning, or launch plans.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Research
use_cases.description: Generate repeatable CSV and Markdown reports for marketplace analysis projects.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One ASIN
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze ASIN B09G9GB4MG and save the reports to ./output.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several ASINs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Amazon ASINs together: B09G9GB4MG, B08N5WRWNW, and B07ABC1111. Summarize price and review differences.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pricing Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the analyzer on these competitor ASINs and highlight the lowest price, highest price, and strongest review profile.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Market Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this ASIN set, generate all report formats, then use the Markdown report to identify product strengths and gaps.

output_examples.input: Analyze three headphone ASINs for price and review strength.
output: A CSV table lists each ASIN, title, brand, price, rating, review count, weight, and features.
A Markdown report shows the price range and top-rated product.
A structured data report preserves raw product results and computed comparisons.

output_examples.input: Create a competitor snapshot for a new product launch.
output_examples.output: The report identifies pricing spread, rating leaders, review volume leaders, and visible feature differences for the supplied ASINs.

output_examples.input: Export Amazon competitor data for spreadsheet review.
output_examples.output: The skill saves a spreadsheet-friendly file with core product fields and a separate written report for review.

best_practices: Use environment variables for the BrowserAct API key instead of command-line arguments.
Run analysis on a focused set of comparable ASINs for clearer price and review signals.
Save each run to a unique output directory to preserve earlier reports.
anti_patterns: Do not run the skill without checking BrowserAct account limits and API usage costs.
Do not treat scraped product data as final without reviewing source page quality.
Do not store reports with sensitive client research in shared directories.

faq.question: What API key does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a BrowserAct API key in the BROWSERACT_API_KEY environment variable.

faq.question: Does it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. It must call the BrowserAct workflow API to collect product data.

faq.question: What inputs does it accept?
faq.answer: It accepts one or more 10-character Amazon ASIN values.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It can create CSV, Markdown, and structured data reports named amazon_analysis in the output directory.

faq.question: Can it analyze review sentiment deeply?
faq.answer: No. The included code compares ratings and review counts, but does not perform advanced sentiment analysis.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
